## Proof

Let $f$ be meromorphic on $\mathbb{C}$ with $|f(z)\,z^{2}|\le 1$ for $|z|\ge 1$, i.e. $|f(z)|\le |z|^{-2}$ there.

**Step 1 — All poles lie in $\overline{\mathbf{D}}{}^{\,c}$-complement, i.e. inside $|z|<1$.**
For $|z|\ge 1$ we have $|f(z)|\le 1$, so $f$ is bounded (hence holomorphic, no poles) on $\{|z|\ge 1\}$. Thus every pole of $f$ lies in the compact set $\{|z|<1\}$; being isolated with no accumulation point in $\mathbb{C}$, there are only **finitely many** poles. Consequently $f$ extends to a meromorphic function on the Riemann sphere $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$, i.e. $f$ is rational.

**Step 2 — Behavior at infinity.**
Since $|f(z)|\le |z|^{-2}\to 0$ as $z\to\infty$, the point $\infty$ is a removable singularity of $f$ with $f(\infty)=0$. Moreover $|z^{2}f(z)|\le 1$ for $|z|\ge 1$ says $z^{2}f(z)$ is bounded near $\infty$, so $f(z)=O(z^{-2})$ as $z\to\infty$. Hence the Laurent expansion of $f$ at $\infty$ has the form
$$f(z)=\frac{a_{2}}{z^{2}}+\frac{a_{3}}{z^{3}}+\cdots,$$
with **no $z^{-1}$ term**.

**Step 3 — Residue at infinity vanishes.**
By definition $\operatorname{Res}(f,\infty)=-[\text{coefficient of }z^{-1}]$, which is $0$ by Step 2.

**Step 4 — Apply the global residue theorem.**
For a function meromorphic on $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$,
$$\sum_{\text{all poles }p\in\widehat{\mathbb{C}}}\operatorname{Res}(f,p)=0.$$
Splitting off the point at infinity,
$$\sum_{p\in\mathbb{C}}\operatorname{Res}(f,p)=-\operatorname{Res}(f,\infty)=0.$$
By Step 1 every finite pole of $f$ lies in $|z|<1$, so the sum above is exactly the sum of residues inside $\mathbf{D}$.

**Step 5 — Conclude via the residue theorem.**
With $\partial\mathbf{D}$ positively oriented,
$$\int_{\partial\mathbf{D}} f(z)\,dz = 2\pi i\sum_{|p|<1}\operatorname{Res}(f,p)=2\pi i\cdot 0 = 0.$$

$$\boxed{\displaystyle\int_{\partial\mathbf{D}} f(z)\,dz = 0.}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
